blocks.text: Trẻ trâu (translated into "young buffalo") is a rebellious, punk/hipster-like subculture in Vietnam that emerged in the late 2000s to late 2010s, with the term describing reckless, impulsive, and loud youth. It is often associated with an informal street youth or counter-public subculture known for late-night motorbike riding without helmets, breaking the rules, gaudy/tacky fashion, going to parties for techno/electronic music, rebellious behavior, and provocative online actions.

The main focus of the subculture features speeding, modified underbone motorcycles, such as Hondas, a spiky hair/swooped fringe appearance, and defiance of traffic laws, characterized by showing off, emotional volatility, rejection of mainstream societal advice, and a hunger for attention. They were most likely active on social media with an ability for dramatic arguments online, provocative comments and flexing, more similar to Dek Waen, Shamate, and Ah Beng.

The whole Tre Trau subculture is most likely hated by mainstream norms due to their toxic behavior, encouraging people to smoke/drink and stealing money to buy products that link to overconsumerism, associating it with the Punk culture for their impulsive mindset and actions, but both are distinct since the Trẻ trâu subculture is known for being apolitical among the youth despite their rebellious attitude in contrast.
